summary: The core fix this task exists for -- a single flock-backed dispatch_core.py concurrency gate shared by dispatch-tick.py, phase-continuation-tick.py, and status-remediation-tick.py, replacing 3 previously independent/uncapped worker-spawn code paths -- is sound, correctly holds the lock across the check-then-spawn critical section, and is proven under real multi-process contention by test_dispatch_core_concurrency_real_processes_enforce_shared_cap (all 18 tests pass). The 6 superseded scripts are renamed (not deleted) with real git history preserved, and the 3 new scripts faithfully preserve the original sub-behaviors (gap_queue_paused gate, module dependency graph, phase-plan merged-PR cross-check, tier2 self-report backfill, mechanical vs judgment-needed remediation classification) unchanged. However, I found and reproduced a real correctness bug in the accompanying superboss-register.py schema change: dispatch_core._upsert_wiring_row() calls sbr._ensure_wiring_registry_table(conn), which is only a CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS no-op on an existing table -- it never calls the new _migrate_wiring_registry_entity_types()/_migrate_schema() that actually widens the wiring_registry CHECK constraint to allow 'dispatch_event'. I built a fixture DB with the literal pre-existing CHECK constraint (matching what the commit message itself says the live 7000+-row production DB has) and confirmed record_dispatch_event() raises 'CHECK constraint failed: entity_type IN (...)' on every call, silently swallowed by the best-effort try/except. None of the 18 new tests catch this because every test builds a brand-new fixture DB whose freshly-created table already bakes in the widened CHECK from the current WIRING_ENTITY_TYPES tuple -- none seed the actual pre-migration schema. Net effect: in real production, every dispatch_event wiring_registry row this consolidation is supposed to add will silently fail to write, forever, until someone separately runs 'superboss-register.py init' or 'register-entity' (neither of which any of the 3 new scripts or their proposed cron entries do) -- contradicting the commit message's claim that the migration was 'verified ... idempotent' against the real write path. This doesn't affect the dispatch-safety fix itself (which doesn't depend on wiring_registry), but it is a confirmed, silent defect in claimed-verified code that undermines the task's own audit-trail/traceability goal, so I'm rejecting pending a fix (e.g. have _upsert_wiring_row call sbr.init_db_silent() or sbr._migrate_schema(conn) before writing, not just _ensure_wiring_registry_table) and a test that seeds the real pre-migration schema.
issues: CONFIRMED: dispatch_core._upsert_wiring_row() (scripts/dispatch_core.py) only calls superboss-register.py's _ensure_wiring_registry_table() (a bare CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS), never init_db()/init_db_silent()/_migrate_schema() -- so the new _migrate_wiring_registry_entity_types() CHECK-widening migration added to scripts/superboss-register.py never runs against a pre-existing production DB. Reproduced directly: building a DB with the literal pre-consolidation CHECK constraint (no 'dispatch_event' value) and calling dispatch_core.record_dispatch_event() raises sqlite3 'CHECK constraint failed', caught and swallowed by the best-effort except-block, so the row is silently never written. Every dispatch_event audit row this consolidation is meant to produce will fail silently in production until someone runs a separate CLI path (init/register-entity) that nothing in this diff's own automation invokes.

None of the 18 new tests exercise a DB seeded with the actual pre-existing schema (they all start from an empty DB, so the freshly-created table already has the widened CHECK baked in from the current code's WIRING_ENTITY_TYPES tuple) -- this gap in test coverage is exactly why the bug above wasn't caught before this review.

Minor/pre-existing, not introduced by this task: dispatch-tick.py's module_queue_tick() iterates candidates module-by-module (all of one module's NEW items before the next module's), so if the shared cap is reached mid-way through one module's queue, later modules get zero slots that tick -- this contradicts the 'round-robin across module queues so one module can't starve another' comment inherited verbatim from the original module-queue-dispatcher.py, which had the identical non-interleaved behavior despite the comment. Worth a follow-up since the consolidation was an opportunity to fix it, but not a regression from this task.
